# Notifications

What the product says back, and where: a Flag for what happened, a Banner for a condition, a SectionMessage for something to act on, and the Inbox for what arrived over time.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Notifications/Notifications.mdx`

## The carriers

Four components carry every message. Each component page holds its appearances; this pattern picks the carrier and the place. A Modal is the fifth, for the one message that must be answered first.

- **Flag.** A passing notice at the top right, two lines at most. Routine ones leave on their own; warning and error stay until acted on.
- **Banner.** A condition that holds for the whole Frame, page or Section: one line, no dismiss, one at a time.
- **SectionMessage.** Something to read or act on that belongs to this part of the page and stays until resolved or dismissed.
- **The Inbox.** Updates that arrived over time, in a 360-wide (`--inbox-width`) Panel beside the Sidebar with `Unread` and `All` tabs and `NotificationItem` rows grouped by day.

## Banner tiers

One banner at a time, scrolling with its content. The Frame tier is system news and pins only during an active outage. The Page tier is about this page. The Section tier is about this collection. The Frame and Page `banner` slots are Planned : today a Banner goes in the content, set where its tier says.

- **Frame.** System news across the whole width, above the Sidebar and the page.
- **Page.** Under the page header, about this page.
- **Section.** At the top of one collection, about that collection.

## Usage

Use Notifications when the product needs to tell someone something: an action finished, a condition holds, a decision is needed. Match the disruption to the urgency: a Flag passes, a SectionMessage stays in the page, a Banner holds for a condition, a Modal interrupts. Keep notifications to what is needed; when every message shouts, none does.

| The message is about… | Carrier | Where | Leaves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Something that already happened and needs no reply: saved, sent, copied | `Flag` | Top right | On its own after 8 s, or Dismiss on a default flag; a bold warning or error when its action resolves it |
| A job that finished after the person moved on | Default `Flag` with an action, `autohide={false}` | Top right | Dismiss, or the action |
| A job that failed after the person moved on | Bold error `Flag` with Try again | Top right | When Try again resolves it; no Dismiss |
| Something to read or act on in this part of the page | `SectionMessage` | Top of the Section or form | Resolved or dismissed |
| Guidance before a task that must not be missed | `SectionMessage`, dismiss off | By the action it informs | When it stops applying |
| A condition that holds for everything in a Frame, page or Section | `Banner` at that tier | Top of the tier | When the condition ends |
| A note beside one thing that most people never need | `InlineMessage` | Beside the field or value | On close |
| Something that must be answered before going on | `Modal`, Acknowledge or Active | Centered over a Backdrop | On the button |
| What arrived over time | The Inbox, a 360-wide (`--inbox-width`) Panel beside the Sidebar | Start of the page, over content, no Backdrop | Escape, outside click, or Close |

## Alternatives

- For an error about one field, put it on the field; see Errors.
- For a state on one object, use a `StatusTag`; see Indicators.
- For a copy confirmation, use the "Copied" tooltip; see Common actions.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Flag title names the event: "Session logged." | "Success!" |
| Flag line gives the next step: "Maya's supervisor will see it Friday." | A bare title with no next step. |
| Banner is one sentence: "Scheduled maintenance Saturday 2–4 AM ET." | A paragraph in the Banner. |
| Own the problem: "We lost the connection. Your work is kept on this device." | "Connection lost by client." |
| Actions are verbs: "Undo", "View sessions". | "Click here", "OK". |

## Accessibility

- Warning and error Flags are alerts and interrupt; every other Flag is a polite status. Each is read as one message.
- A `SectionMessage` announces assertively when it appears; one present at first paint is ordinary content.
- A `Banner` is a status that never traps focus and sits in the reading order.
- The timeout on a Flag is a timing limit; the dismiss × on a default Flag satisfies it (see the Flag page).
- The appearance icon is decorative; the words carry the severity.
- Each `NotificationItem` in the Inbox is one link whose accessible name announces `"Unread"` while unread, with `"Mark as read"` as a sibling button outside the link.

## Related

- Errors: use for where a failure shows.
- Loading: use for the Flag past 10 s.
- Indicators: use for the count on the Bell.

- Modal: use for what must be answered first.

- `Flag`, `Banner`, `SectionMessage`, `InlineMessage`, `NotificationItem`, `Modal`: the components.

## Motion

Notifications reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| flag-enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | A Flag enters from the top right. |
| flag-timeout | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-exit` | A Flag that times out exits the way it came. |
| flag-dismiss | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A Flag closed by hand does a quick fade in place. |
| stack | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The stack closes up when a Flag leaves. |
| message | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A SectionMessage or InlineMessage makes room on spatial.fast, then fades in; it reverses on exit. |
| banner | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A Banner pushes the page down on spatial.default, then fades in. |

## Best practices

### Place Flags at the top right, two lines at most. {#place-flags-at-the-top-right-two-lines-at-most}

**Checked:** Review

A title that names the event and one line for the next step. A `FlagGroup` stacks them in the order you pass them, so pass the newest first, and renders with the page so each one is announced. `FlagGroup` sits at the top right (`top-end`) by default.

### Offer Undo on a Flag with a timer, and commit when it ends. {#offer-undo-on-a-flag-with-a-timer-and-commit-when-it-ends}

**Checked:** Review

An archive or a delete confirms with a Flag that has `timer` and Undo as its first action, instead of a confirmation dialog first. The change commits in `onDismiss`, once. Pressing Undo replaces the Flag with a plain "restored" Flag. Hovering or focusing the Flag pauses the countdown, so reading it never costs the chance to undo.

### Put nothing important only in a Flag. {#put-nothing-important-only-in-a-flag}

**Checked:** Review

A Flag can be dismissed before it is read. A failure that needs a decision stays on the page in a SectionMessage; a decision that blocks the task is a Modal.

Do: A finished action on the default Flag: the event in the title, the next step below.
Don't: A decision in a Flag, which is gone before it is answered.

### Let routine Flags leave and keep warning and error until acted on. {#let-routine-flags-leave-and-keep-warning-and-error-until-acted-on}

**Checked:** Automatic

Normal, information and success close after 8 s. Warning and error never close themselves and offer a next action. On a default, information or success Flag with an action, set `autohide={false}` when the person must act; warning and error ignore it. The × and the rest of the dismiss rule are on the Flag page.

### Show one Banner at a time, one line, at the tier it concerns, for as long as the condition holds. {#show-one-banner-at-a-time-one-line-at-the-tier-it-concerns-for-as-long-as-the-condition-holds}

**Checked:** Automatic

Frame for system news, pinned only during an active outage ; Page for this page; Section for this collection. A Banner has no dismiss and no timeout, so it is mounted only while the condition is true, and it scrolls with the content.

Do: One Banner, one line, at the tier it concerns.
Don't: Two Banners stacked, pushing the page down.

### Keep a SectionMessage in the page until it is resolved or dismissed. {#keep-a-sectionmessage-in-the-page-until-it-is-resolved-or-dismissed}

**Checked:** Automatic

The fill and icon carry the appearance, with no border and no side stripe. A blocking message turns dismiss off. Put up to two actions after the body. Field errors stay on the field.

### Match the appearance to the meaning and say it in the words. {#match-the-appearance-to-the-meaning-and-say-it-in-the-words}

**Checked:** Review

Success for a finished action, warning for a caution, danger only when something failed. The icon is hidden from screen readers, so the title says "saved", "couldn't", "due".

### Keep routine news on the default Flag. {#keep-routine-news-on-the-default-flag}

**Checked:** Review

A bold fill competes with the page; it is for what must be seen. Routine news stays on the default Flag, which the person can clear.

### Send what arrived over time to the Inbox. {#send-what-arrived-over-time-to-the-inbox}

**Checked:** Review

A Flag is for now; the Inbox is for later. The Inbox opens from the Sidebar at `--inbox-width` over the start of the page with no Backdrop, carrying `Mark all as read`, settings and close in the header, `Unread` (with count) and `All` tabs, and `NotificationItem` rows grouped by day. Clearing every unread item shows `"You are all caught up."` in `EmptyState`; pressing `Escape` or clicking outside closes the panel.
